newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain cannot collect 200 bln pta in lapsed taxes.
newsitem.headline: Spain cannot collect 200 bln pta in lapsed taxes.

text.p: Spain can no longer collect more than 200 billion pesetas in outstanding contested taxes as the cases have now lapsed, Secretary of the Exchequer Juan Costa said on Tuesday.
Costa blamed mismanagement and "unjustified delays" from the previous Socialist administration for the lapsed cases.
He said the amount referred to about 600 tax cases, which can no longer be claimed. According to Spanish law, contested cases cannot be delayed by more than six months.
In February 1996, the High Court ruled that contested tax monies could not be collected by Hacienda if the enquiry lasted more than six months.
According to a report prepared by the Agencia Tributaria, which collects taxes, there were "totally unjustified" delays of more than two years and in same cases, of more than five years.

"As a result, Hacienda and all Spanish citiziens will no longer be able to collect more than 200 billion pesetas in taxes because of the lack of efficiency and of responsibility of the previous team," Costa told journalists.
Costa explained that the cases referred to income and corporate taxes, and that the delays were due to a lack of organisation and to the lack of personnel.
He also noted that since May 1996, when the new government took power, not a single case has been lost to delays.
Costa said he would request an appearance before parliament to adopt measures to rule out further similar cases.
Spain has never taken into account this money in its budget, and this money will not affect the deficit, Costa ended.
